Birdocracy||Poem.text:
Birds are free to do as they please,
Are we free to do as we please?
Birds can go here and there;
We can go here but not there.
Birds cannot cry but they do fly;
We cannot fly but we do cry.
I heard a man the other day:
He said birds killed for food.
I heard a bird the other day:
He said men killed for fun.
We have laws, but they always are broken;
Birds have naught, and nothing’s ever broken.
Men look to the sky and think there is heaven,
Birds fly to the sky and rise above our lies!

Fast to Get Away From the Past||Poem.text:
This thought of mine lingers in my head as I get up from bed,
It even gets stronger as I look in the mirror, I get a shiver:
What did I do for which I need to hide?
What has caused this stupid long ride?
This thing, for which I lied and I cried?
The answer is as I thought:
My fault is naught!

Solitude||Poem.text:
Solitude is a desolate experience none should suffer,
And only the devil might beg to differ.
Imagine yourself lost in the woods, for eternity,
Forever and ever until it becomes your reality.
Suffocation creeps up your throat because you wanna talk,
But no one’s around and all you can do is walk.
The borders of reality begin to fade around you;
You start speaking to yourself as only a madman would do.
You’re lonely and tired of searching;
Your heart is empty and hurting.
You start imagining friends and a different place;
You’re eager and walk at a faster pace.
But sanity comes back to your head,
And a few tears you must shed.
Imagine no friends, no play, no laughs.
Imagine the cries, the hate, the fights.
A world without love, imagine,
But one only full of sin.

Come Back||Poem.text:
Everything’s the same.
You try to stay in the game,
But eventually you lose the ball,
And then comes the fall.
You try to get back on your feet,
Because you just can’t admit defeat,
But for the rise you need the strength,
You need the force to go the length.

Claire||Poem.text:
The game of life is unfair,
An endless spiral of tricky affair.
But all hell’s not loose and ablare;
I hope and try not to despair,
Because there are things I could dare.
I could breathe in some sweet air,
Try and give her a stare,
Or even gently brush her hair.
I’ll lure her to my lair,
And mine she’ll be there,
But beware, Claire’s not to share!

Untitled 1||Poem.text:
Eventuality is scary,
Yet surprisingly,
A reality to me
And to thee!

Second Chance||Poem.text:
Life is dim,
And chances slim,
But hope within,
And you can win!

The Forbidden Place||Poem.text:
In the Forbidden Place,
I hide my face,
And dare not say grace.

My muscles crisp as I enter through the door,
And my body trembles to the creaking floor,
I’ve never been afraid like this before,
I’ll enter the Forbidden Place no more.

In that cold, cold room,
Waiting in my tomb,
Is something called doom.

I muster some courage and venture deeper,
My legs shake and my heart beats faster,
Footsteps in the distance, I shiver.
He says, “Bow down to your eternal master.”

To him I won’t lie,
But from fear I do cry,
Wishing away I could fly.

Desperate, I look around for the exit.
Such a distance, I ponder if I should dare it,
He’s a powerful monster, I’ll never make it.
Over my fate I have no control, so let it be it.

Away I do race,
To the fastest possible pace,
From the Forbidden Place.

¿Existence?||Poem.text:
Never forget you’re not blind,
And your own way you can find.

Never forget you’ve got a mind,
The others don’t follow behind.

There are some who say He exists,
Some who hit with closed fists.
But these people, the real joy of life they do miss,
If He does exist, what’s the point for all this?
This man’s father died earlier today,
This man’s brother his food he couldn’t pay.
The lies I hear, the lies they say,
To this propaganda our minds are in slow decay.

Remember, there’s no one but us on this Earth,
So to a new era we shall give birth!

Still Standing||Poem.text:
I doubt and I doubt,
And I look up and about.
All I want to do is shout,
But don’t count me out.
You may be right, I might be dead,
Yet I see the light and raise my head.
My apocalypse is far,
I live life like a shooting star,
Always staying above par,
Because I aim high and far!

Wake Up||Poem.text:
Open your eyes to the whys and its lies,
Our world lies near hell, slowly it dies.
That frightened man, away he flies,
Away, from the worst and their cries.
And I can’t see the rise, but realize,
That we need to mobilize,
And Evil we’ll hypnotize!

The Child||Poem.text:
Whose voice is it that cries inside of me,
When all around, here and there, is misery?
We all see but none of us act,
As if apathy was a secret pact.
We’re all prisoners in confinement,
Ignorant and indifferent!

Seven Heaven||Poem.text:
I’m blocked in my shell
At the footstep of hell.
Behind me is heaven,
Population: seven
There’s Lady D, and Kennedy,
Microsoft Billy and Mother T.,
The King Jr. of equality,
That skinny Indy, Gandhi,
And there’s Lincoln, don’t you see?
All so good, unlike me!

Vulnerable||Poem.text:
I’m indifferent about loneliness,
I’m independent yet feel no happiness.
There aren’t many things for which I care,
But I’m weak when upon me I feel her stare!

Doubt||Poem.text:
Words are not to be trusted,
Because they can be twisted.
The truth has been tried,
And in the end I cried.

Hope||Poem.text:
“Are you the man I fear?”
And he sizzled, “Yes, my dear!”
For a minute all I could do was stare,
Then the stranger revealed his head bare.
Instead of black he had fading gray hair,
And his look was not scary, in fact there was nothing there.
“You can’t be the man I fear,” I said,
“You can’t be the monster underneath my bed.”

A Last Cry Out for Redemption||Poem.text:
I’ve lost my faith in you, dear,
And there’s nothing I can do, you hear?
You must move yourself, or I fear,
Not once for you shall I shed a tear!

Patience||Poem.text:
The river flows and he moves not,
No matter if the sun strikes hot.
Fully awake, his love he awaits,
And in his mind linger many debates.

The farmer’s clock suddenly chimes noon.
His heart despairs not, she’ll come soon.
His desire is stronger than his appetite,
But sadness glooms in the absence of light.

If patience is a virtue,
Then to him many respects are due.
Lightning strikes, yet he stays, bold,
Sitting under the moon’s nightly cold,
Because next morning he might just strike gold.

Reincarnation||Poem.text:
Broken promises are my eternal enemies,
Yet so many people do they appease.
If only once I could hear the truth I need,
Reassurance for a new life, a new seed,
Like a newborn baby a father pledges to feed,
Like a rich man’s resolution to stop his greed,
I promise, in turn,
That my past I would burn,
From scratch I would rise,
I would send away those stupid lies,
I would accomplish my dreams,
Rediscover those striking beams.
My confusion would dissipate,
And so much more, all on a silver plate!

Exodus||Poem.text:
Loathing effect is in order,
Insanity nears my border,
Harder, faster,
Time moves on,
But my soul is gone!

Last Regards||Poem.text:
As I leaf through my past,
Memories fill my heart!
A new friendship I hope will last,
A love with whom I had to part,
Lines full of lies,
Yet lies define my truth.
I have pained to find excitement,
But I was not hasteful to despair.
I will not rot in peace nor will I rest in hell!
I only have one advice for you in life,
Then you can roll the dice and get a wife:
Don’t judge a book by its cover,
Cliffnotes do it faster!

Is Hope Needful?||Poem.text:
I hear a no, and my heart is full of disillusionment.
It’s a no go, yet again a new disappointment.
That girl was a no show, pain and disenchantment.

Hope floats through time until it hits a brick wall,
But without hope, could you live another tomorrow?

Follow the flow of the river of hope
By paving your own way through the field of destiny.

Opened Eyes||Poem.text:
I ponder about the past,
And wonder about the future,
But today’s air isn’t pure,
And tomorrow won’t bring any more sunshine.
Those dark hovering clouds will not dissipate,
Nor will they let me control my fate,
So I grow old and full of hate,
But I learn the worst I must anticipate,
And I rejoice at the miracles of life.
The world is cold, I’ve been told,
But of its people a better image I hold.

Vonnegut||Poem.text:
History, read it and weep!
But dwell not on our errors deep,
And awaken us from this profound sleep,
That we may climb this hill of time so steep,
And no more again act like a herd of sheep!

Deceived||Poem.text:
Life is full of ephemeral thrills,
Of unclimbed hills.
It could be eternally harmonious,
Even luxurious.
But in reality those things I do not see,
Instead spreads misery and poverty.

Bits and Pieces of my Life||Poem.text:
Reminiscence of joyous memories is eternal happiness,
But I regret the lost times won over by the evil of sadness!
The harshness of life is ephemeral when in my profound sleep,
I dream and dream about heartful moments,
But then I awaken to heartless times,
To this world that we all regret and disown but dare not change!
Oh, I regret!
I wish I could muster some courage and grow some muscles,
Or have a magic toy with which to whistle!
Then time could stop and listen to reason instead of giving it a deaf ear!
How life could be sweet and dear right here on this Earth,
But instead I fear of all the evils I hear!
All the sirens at the gates of hell go ablare,
Because it’s near, our apocalypse!
We’re attacked at the front and the rear;
Will no one stand up to save mankind?
Do we not each have a mind,
Or are we looking for more excuses to find,
To pretend all is well?
Do we not each have our eyes,
Are we all so blind?
The darkening clouds that gloom over our fate,
Soon our memories will dissipate,
And open the gate to replace love by hate!
But if those dark clouds appear,
If my memories disappear,
I will lose what I hold dear,
I will lose my source of life,
So might as well stick in me a knife!

5 Million Bucks for Nothing||Poem.text:
Oh say can you see,
By the dawn’s early light!

Seagulls by the sea,
Leave on an abrupt flight!

While men try to plea,
Away the devil’s fright!

But nothing scares me,
Not this satanic sight!

So this is my fee,
If you want me to fight!

If you want me to fight,
This will be my fee!

Rest in Hell or…||Poem.text:
I am full of chagrin for the lonely assassin.
That solitary man who sits alone, with no phone.
His head thickens with regrets on lost bets,
No children, no wife, not even some pets.
Sitting in a chair, smoking a cigar,
Thinking of what to share, with whom to go far.
But that letter comes in with this envelope,
And he opens it like a stupid big dope!
He keeps falling on the slippery slope,
And he remembers a childhood hope!
He dreamed of space and astronauts,
But along the way there were too many faults!
He loads a bullet into his gun,
While watching kids having such fun!
He wakes up from this momentary lapse,
He returns to his monotonous life because perhaps,
On this last hour of détente before his assignment,
He prays he will be caught,
So in heaven he can rot!

Indifference||Poem.text:
It’s rare to see someone fair,
Not to see someone scared,
To see someone dare.
Just know there’s enough wealth to share,
But not enough people around who care!

Joy||Poem.text:
Crack a smile once in a while,
Coz life moves on, love is not gone,
It’s just absent, be persistent!

Subway Experience||Poem.text:
Sadman was once a young man,
But now no one gives a damn!
His hopes were crushed by misery, his life a tragedy,
But no one feels sorry for him,
Because our vision is dim,
Our actions so lame,
That I can only feel shame.
This desperate man asked for sympathy,
But we showed him no mercy.
Our silence in complicity with our indifference
Explains our world’s decadence,
Because in the end Sadman cried in his seat,
As if we’d beat him with our feet.
The slim chance for light to shine,
For love to return to its joyous shrine,
Was that after our intolerable act,
Because of Sadman’s unbearable cries,
Which pierced our hearts,
The beasts were no longer there,
And we showed we sometimes are people who care!

Loyalty||Poem.text:
It is not bought, it is deserved.
But once acquired,
It cannot be sold, it must be kept.
Do you accept?

Here and Now||Poem.text:
Maybe yesterday there was a chance,
Maybe tomorrow there’ll be new hope,
But today I drift away,
Nowhere else I’d rather stay!

Wrecked||Poem.text:
I’m like a deceived bird,
Afraid of voices heard,
Wanting to fly away,
But my wings are stuck at bay!
I try to rise above,
Can’t bear no cries of love,
But I ran out of luck,
I’m cooked like a sitting duck!

The Rise||Poem.text:
Plenty of tears I’ll shed,
In the years ahead.
You see, my heart bled,
My shirt’s stained red,
As if the rain poured down,
And the lion roared as I drowned.
I was alone in my misery,
Listening to lies and hypocrisy,
And I paid the fee,
But now the light I see;
The brick wall shattered,
And you shivered,
To the truth I uttered!

Desire||Poem.text:
The fire of fears
Compelled to ashes
By the passion of tears,
The dust of lust,
Of pleasures lost,
And undesired love,
Swept away
By the thought
Of such
A tender touch!

Life||Poem.text:
Life is full of insurmountable obstacles,
Of brusquely opened doors,
Of flashing emergency signs,
Resulting in abrupt and impatient decisions,
Of resurging problems of helpless causes,
Of dashed hopes and seeked redemptions!

Life is empty of normality,
Of tranquil flow of actions,
Of peaceful negotiations and undisturbed waters!
Never did such a No Man’s Land stay unviolated!

Life is a little boy knocking on a gigantic door,
Anxiously waiting for the answer,
Only to discover that there is none!

Armed and Dangerous||Poem.text:
I was once a young boy with aspiring dreams,
Thinking we could all fairly come to our means,
But now I’m full of dashed hopes and faded jeans,
Like all those stupid washed out teens.
Widowed kings never went looking for new queens,
So why should I look for new means?

Wrong Choice||Poem.text:
My road alters, I follow a new trail,
My hope falters, my body feels so frail!

Incredulity||Poem.text:
That cynic man,
That twisted guy,
Who made this Earth,
And the untainted sky,
Who made man walk,
And made birds fly,
He made men lie,
And babies cry,
He made you sly,
And made me shy,
That twisted guy,
Who’ll make me die,
I have my doubts,
I must ask, why?

Sin City||Poem.text:
Followers pray
On this saddening day,
And tomorrow,
There’ll be sorrow,
Yet we don’t know,
Where shall he go!

Corrupted||Poem.text:
I was the one-eyed king from the kingdom of the blinds,
Lost everything because they had freedom on their minds.
Now a sinner in search of the land where the sun shines,
My redemption’s stuck at the juncture of borderlines;
My cause is lost, my Eden fades ‘till I see the signs.
But then the sane, harmonious presence of light declines,
And I’m taunted with a treasure chest not worth two dimes,
My weakened self loses the good fight, my soul resigns!

Death||Poem.text:
I listen attentively but I only hear the clock ticking.
I put my hand to my chest but can’t feel my heart beating.
My nostrils twitch to a reeking smell that slowly creeps in,
The future looks grim!
I don’t feel any wound or infuriating pain,
But I notice the opened gash and the bloodstain.
Then I realize I’m looking down at my lifeless body,
My soul, my mind is full of agony,
My concealed serenity turns to panic,
There’s an anomaly because I’m not sick!
I acknowledge the fact that I am dead,
How I regret the life I’ve led.
But I embrace the impatient truth I hoped:
The sky’s empty, men have been doped!

Lost||Poem.text:
Innocence is dead,
My secrets have fled!
A consolation, I said,
Soothe my aching head,
But desperation, I dread,
Will haunt me instead!

Desolation||Poem.text:
I want to sing to thee my affinity,
But you mistrust my sincerity,
Ignore my sentiments,
And deplore my compliments!
I’m deprived of any hope,
My life falling on a downward slope,
Light fading away,
Darkness finding its way!

Perseverance||Poem.text:
I clinch to my dreams of old,
Dashed as they may be in this world so cold,
And I try to be bold, not to fold,
Because my pride can’t be sold,
Even in this world so cold!

¿Tolerance?||Poem.text:
The blasphemous priest never liked girls,
He preferred men with earrings and pearls.
He kept his secret because he knew what it’d mean.
But one day he was seen with a gay magazine!
Then started the glances from his friends and his peers,
The end of his career was near, it gave him many fears!
He quit because he couldn’t accept his fate,
But to start over it was too late!
And now he ponders in the gutters,
Listening to the ghostly utters,
And suddenly his mind cracks,
Envy, motivation, he just lacks!
Deprived of his faith yesterday,
He understands today!

Dreamland||Poem.text:
I’ve been here before,
To this land I adore,
This place you deplore.
It’s this kingdom of mine,
Where all have a free mind,
Where I come every night,
At the decline of light!
And what joy I get,
From this marvelous sight!
Smiles stuck to faces,
Lies flock from all places!
It’s an escape from your world of misery;
At my arrival problems vanish quickly!
But you’re not welcomed with your bag of dirt,
Because then someone might just get hurt,
So if you want to join my nightmares,
Then you’ve got so much time to spare!

Departure||Poem.text:
Alleviate the pain,
That though leaves a burden such!
Must you leave a stain,
That nevertheless hurts so much?
Because when light last shone,
And felt my sunken heart,
Death came alone,
To tear me apart!

Sophie||Poem.text:
My story here it starts,
Listen all you lonely hearts,
There was an amazing girl
As beautiful as a pearl!
I’d run a whole smile,
Just to see her smile,
To touch her glistening hair,
And feel her knock-out stare!
She was the lump in my throat,
The hole in my boat,
Because although I loved her,
I knew I couldn’t have her!
To pronounce her name
Filled me with shame,
Because I wasn’t worthy
To whisper, “Sophie…”

Repentance||Poem.text:
Old skin was once strong,
A burly man with a quick mind!
He knew life was long,
And he always tried to be kind!

Old skin never forgot
When Sophie came to town,
How hard he had fought
So she’d give him the crown!

Old skin had a drink,
And misbehaved, no fret!
But when later he could think,
Oh, such regret!

Old skin, life of despair,
Sophie all but suffered!
Her man didn’t treat her fair,
He tried but blundered!

Old skin had not cried
When Sophie’d gone away,
Because although she’d died,
In his heart she would stay!

Old skin, the yung’uns said,
When they saw his wrinkled body,
And inside he bled,
His pain at God’s mercy!

Old skin, weak bones,
Empty heart, dried tears,
In his bed he twists and moans,
Compelled to live haunted by fears!

Old skin was once young,
But now he can’t remember,
How sweet is the old song
About the girl so tender!

Struggle||Poem.text:
Faded light recedes,
My familiar solitude proceeds,
Terrorizing Darkness grows!
The Red River of Death,
Where man gasped his last breath,
In it my poisoned blood flows!

But in the distant horizon,
The constant sun’s arisin’
And new hope, rejoice!
The battle is ephemeral,
Yet the war eternal!
Alas, I’ve made my choice!

Utopia||Poem.text:
Faraway, the distant land of constant day,
Faraway, nowhere near, destroys my fear,
Faraway, yeah, yeah, yeah, from the city of sin!
Faraway, yeah, yeah, yeah, no more chagrin!

Faraway, faraway, to the constant day!
Faraway, battled night, defeated fright,
Faraway, to the soundless sleep, to the safest sleep,
Faraway, from the ocean’s deep, from the children’s weep,

Faraway, the sacred place, far today, out of space!

Claustrophobia||Poem.text:
My words float through space,
Bounce back against the wall.
I’m contained in this hollow place,
A spectator to my own fall!
I’m drained of energy,
In search of a remedy;
I dread the night, the desperate sleep,
I try and try yet always weep!

Subway Experience 2||Poem.text:
I feel no fear,
And fear no one!
I’m an anxious boy
Awaiting the next time,
As if life was a toy
And vengeance not a crime!
I’ll be ready,
With boiling energy,
And no one will hold me back
Because motivation I don’t lack!
The urge is lame,
Yet not for fame;
It’s more profound,
Like a silent sound
Deep down inside of me
Waiting to burst out!

Undirected||Poem.text:
I’m lost,
But don’t know where I’m going!
The road
Is icy and long and curling!
The woods
Are seeping through and expanding!
The past is blurry,
And the future gloomy,
And I don’t know where I’m going!
The sky is cloudy,
And the darkness scary!
My feet
Are hurt and pained and fleeing!
My skin
Is old and wrinkled and peeling!
My heart
Is empty and lonely and dying!
My memories are fading,
And I don’t know where I’m going!

The Master and the Serf||Poem.text:
Two men were walking through obscure woods,
One well-dressed, the other carrying the goods!
The servant was leading the way because he knew the territories,
Though he was ignorant of today’s equalities.
The master was content with his manly possession,
And gladder still of his envied position.
He was meeting a woman he would prosper and marry,
Though because of his greed he would cheat daily.
His union was not for love, t’was for land and money,
And he did not care if she would ever be merry!
The serf had a woman he cherished,
And she would cry if he perished!
His intentions were noble though his stature was not;
His whole life in poverty he would rot.
But though it was the master who had all the riches of the world,
The servant was happier because he had the loving girl!
On their fifth day of traveling, burdened with fatigue,
Both men experienced a vision of intrigue.
The master was scared when he saw the black crow,
His face going livid of trepidation to the apparition of his foe,
While the serf rejoiced at the arrival of the dove,
Bringing reminisce of his beautiful love.
Because he was scared, the master was sure,
He needed to do something pure,
Or something terrible would happen to him,
Oh, the future looked grim!
He said, “Serf, I must commit a good deed,
Therefore from now on, you are freed!”
The servant, in his daze of joy,
Remained innocent and coy.
He replied, “Sir, I fear for my sweetheart,
Afraid from this world she might part.
So to protect my pretty darling,
For you I’ll do a good thing.”
And they went on, two men walking through the obscure woods,
One well-dressed, the other carrying the goods!

Alone||Poem.text:
Nobody’s waiting for me, is anyone for you?
Life’s hard, and I ain’t got a clue,
I hear the babies cry and the women crumble,
While I try and try but must always fumble!

It’s always the same for me, is it also for you?
Times are hard, problems accrue,
Love is a maze swathed in a haze,
While I am amazed at its disparate ways!

I hope there’s a place for me, but is there for you?
Life is short, and my time is due,
I have no remorse but one in this cold, old world;
While the ride was coarse I didn’t get me no girl!

Jukebox||Poem.text:
My mind is a machine of reminisce,
But not all dreams are always bliss.
I remember the days of old,
When hate was flat and dry!
I can’t forget those nights so cold,
When you would writhe and cry!
I was often an honest man,
Sometimes a charlatan,
Maybe that’s why you left,
But you stole my heart away;
You committed theft
When you fled that day!
All that remains are memories,
But I don’t linger on the past long;
I let them sail in open seas,
Then I move on to the next song!

Vanished||Poem.text:
I watch the sunrise and realize that I’m alone,
I watch the sky and wonder when light last shone!

I’m scared to be forgotten,
I’m scared of the future,
I’m scared I’ve become rotten,
I’m scared that there’s no cure!

I’d run across the ocean to leave my shell of solitude,
I’d run across time to make life simple and crude!

I’m full of lament,
Tired of holding back the tears,
I’m full of torment,
But ready to confront the fears!

I’m gone but I wish I were still there,
I’m gone but I hope that you still care!

Revolution||Poem.text:
I used to be a foolish clown,
But now there’s something new in town,
Ain’t you scared?

I used to be sad and down,
But now I’ve got the strength and the crown,
Ain’t you scared?

I used to be lost, now I’m found,
I searched long to know where I’m bound,
Ain’t you scared?

The Phantoms||Poem.text:
The phantoms are coming,
Those invisible slimy shapes,
Hiding in the presence of the dark,
Pretending fear is a lark.
They haunt my perturbed mind,
Looking for secrets to find,
And I’m in a frenzied panic,
Afraid of my mysterious past!
The phantoms are coming,
And I yearn for protection,
Like a coward,
My life spiraling downward!
I can’t afford to look back,
I’m too far ahead the track,
And I’m full of fear,
The phantoms are here!

Untitled 2||Poem.text:
Love frustrates me like no other thing
Because I’m afraid of loneliness,
But it won’t keep me down for long,
Because one of these days,
No matter the delays,
I know I’ll meet a girl,
The one from my dreams.
I feel it in my heart deep inside,
So time I’ll patiently abide,
Until the right moment comes along,
From above or below, in front or behind,
I’ll bump into my fantasy and I’ll find,
A life so kind, a love so blind,
That’ll it blow away my mind
And it will become my reality!

Like Always||Poem.text:
I go home alone, like always,
Because solitude is my best friend,
The rain battering down
In the cold heart of the night!

I drink alone, like always,
Because booze is my best friend,
My head spinning around
And my eyes blinded by light!

I remember alone, like always,
Because regret is my worst foe,
The ghosts a whispering sound
And my heart weakened by blight!

I die alone, like always,
Because death is undesired woe,
My soul leaves the ground,
Because of Man’s pitiful spite!

Untitled 3||Poem.text:
Life is hectic at times,
Some days empty.
Today I’m sad,
But tomorrow who knows?
Yesterday I was glad,
Endlessly hopeful,
But today I’m drained,
Searching to ease the heartache
That seems so fake,
So surreal and drowsy.
I’m living in a windowless room,
Over-crowded with unresolved problems
That accrue,
But space doesn’t expand,
It narrows,
And I suffocate from the stress
That lies ahead,
From friends that fled,
But I hear life sometimes is sublime,
Warmth creeping up from light that shines,
But I don’t expect that much;
My hopes are low,
Ready for the devastating blow,
Ready to be surprised,
Ready for the wasted surprise,
Able to confront the lies
And the shrilling cries
That pierce my heart,
And twist it and shred it to pieces;
My perturbed mind battles the boredom,
Fathoms the truth,
And regrets,
Oh,
How it regrets!

Rye, NY||Poem.text:
The ticket home’s expensive,
But I’m motivated, dedicated
To the lost cause,
The hopeless prospect
Of seeing again glazing luxurious cars
Parked in the jovial Main Street,
Over-crowded with coffee shops and barbershops,
Mothers frustrated by their children’s bleat,
Boys sweating because of the summer heat,
Thinking of the fresh coca-cola awaiting in the fridge,
Wishing their ego won’t cringe
(in vain)
When they ask girls out to a movie!
The ticket home’s expensive,
Yes, but worth every penny!

Untitled 4||Poem.text:
I cry for help but they don’t hear.
They can’t, they’re an ocean away,
So I wish I were a wave
That would cross the waters and break on the beach;
Then I would cry out again,
And they would hear me
And liberate me from loneliness,
Clutching me away from its
Entangling arms that surround me
And suffocate me to the point
Where I can’t breathe,
So I hold my breath with ease
And pray with tears pouring down my cheeks,
Hoping to be heard so I can be soothed
And then the pain will cease.
So please, listen,
Because when the wave comes crashing,
I might be crying!

So God Bless||Poem.text:
There’s a binding force that controls us,
Dictates our every move even though we wrote the rules;
At least some people tend to think so.
They jeopardize their freedom
To be enslaved in this kingdom,
But I’m the rebellious teen that defies the laws,
The thinker that won’t crumble to the
Oppressor that you call the Creator,
But what has He created?
A society of greed,
Of innocents who bleed,
Naïve believers who pray in vain
To eradicate the pain and the bloodstain!
So please, explain!
Am I going insane, sick from the pouring rain?
Or are you to blame for your mistake,
Because it’s all fake,
What you pray for and what you hope for,
Because there’s no door that leads to heaven or hell,
There’s only resurging pain, a soar,
Then your body drops to the floor,
Motionless, soulless,
And Earth is a man-less,

Big Brother||Poem.text:
What a hero I am,
With no aspiring dream!
What joy I exert,
Flawed with loneliness!
And I bear the sadness,
The madness, the rage,
And I dread the time
When we will stop to talk,
Because you’ll realize
How empty I am,
And how fake I seem;
You’ll turn your gaze away
In search of another hero!

Untitled 5||Poem.text:
His life is jeopardized
By a disease called loneliness,
An enemy he battled for many years,
But the war is lost,
His life now the cost,
Though he doesn’t regret the fight,
Maybe only the fright,
The fear to die alone,
The mere thought of
Sheer isolation from peers,
Dear madness!
He hates being
Forlorn and abandoned,
Having no one’s shoulder to cry on;
But how was he to be saved
By the valiant white knight
With such a brave front,
An impenetrable façade?
How was he to be helped
By friends and family,
When he remained silent,
Didn’t yell out loud?
The disease,
At the heart of all hearts,
Suddenly betakes him,
And away he parts!
Do you wonder?
Over yonder,
Beyond the sea of clouds
To the ravaging hell,
Beyond the waves of flames
To the pleasant heaven,
His existence becomes a blur
Buried six feet under!
And despite his plea,
Although you regret,
Slowly,
You forget…

Untitled 6||Poem.text:
I weep to forget,
Lost deep in regret,
I weep silently,
So you will not hear,
Quietly at night,
To vanquish my fear,
To clear my thoughts,
And set a tranquil flow
Of river of thoughts
In the land of my mind,
And I weep like the rain,
Pouring unstoppably
But ceasing immediately,
Leaving behind a rainbow,
And you stare, wondering,
At the miraculous colors
And their meanings,
Peaceful, unreal,
Yet you feel light, weightless,
And you rise and fly
Toward the rainbow
And again I weep
When you part,
To forget you’re gone,
To regret the waste
Of time in haste
I blame myself
And so I weep alone
And then you’re gone
And life lasts long
And I forget,
But still, I weep!

Regret||Poem.text:
Why did I push you away?
Now I can’t stop thinking about you,
Your face ever present all day,
My head thickens with regrets that accrue.
I wish I could go back in time
Because I know I won’t have a second chance.
I wish you could forgive me,
But don’t forget me,
Don’t forbid me to see you again,
And don’t pretend you don’t care,
Don’t send me away though you think it’s fair.

Untitled 7||Poem.text:
My exhaustion is pushed away by the thought
Of you that lingers in my head,
It keeps me alive,
That ravishing smile of yours,
How I wish to see it everyday till my last day;
How I enjoyed the tinkling sensation in my stomach
When you leaned close to me and whispered words
That gently brushed past my ears;
Words that are senseless, because I was dazed,
Hypnotized by your presence;
You can’t cease to impress me with the joy you exert;
Looking at you is like looking at one of the world’s seven wonders,
It’s pure beauty;
Have you not noticed my eyes incessantly devouring every inch of your body, because to me, it is perfect?
A perfect body for a perfect girl,
Because that’s what you are,
An amazing girl!
I regret you’re gone,
But most of all,
I regret I didn’t have the guts to tell you one little phrase,
A whisper of three words which could have changed so much,
Which mean so much to me,
The most beautiful phrase invented by mankind:
I love you!
There, I’ve said it.
I know you don’t feel the same way about me,
And I really hope this doesn’t affect our friendship that I cherish so much,
And which I wouldn’t trade for anything in the world,
Because there’s nothing better than you.
I wish with all my heart that you find true happiness,
Wherever that may lead you,
Because you deserve the best, and nothing else.
My only hope is that one day I see you again,
If only for a minute, and nothing else,
Because I love you,
And nothing else!

Dreams||Poem.text:
I am the hunter of dreams,
Because dreams tell the truth, don’t they?
I am the cleanser of screams,
Because screams are unworthy of dreams, aren’t they?

I move forth with extreme rapidity,
Because dreams vanish from the mind,
To be lost in eternity,
Like the sight of the blind.

I collect them in a bag,
Like a bag of bones but a bag of dreams,
The concocted result has no tag,
Has no purpose, it seems.

But I know its importance,
Because many a morning I have forgotten my dreams,
Let alone their significance,
So I rejoice when I fumble through my bag of dreams.

I am the hunter of dreams,
The cleanser of screams,
So will thee ask to see,
Act on that curiosity?

Come forth and give thy hand,
And next to me shall you stand,
So your body rightly leans,
And look deep in the bag of dreams.

Tom (screenplay; working title)||Screenp.text:
EXT.  COMMONWEALTH AVE, BOSTON - NIGHT
Tom, a 19-year-old kid, is waiting in the middle of the street for the T-train, under the pouring rain.  In one arm he is holding a radio, in the other an overstuffed luggage.  His torn sneakers and clothes are drenched.  A car stops at a red light, pulling up almost next to Tom.  In the car are four kids: two boys and two girls.  One of the boys, the driver, with an arm over one of the girls’ shoulders, turns and looks at Tom.  The boy grins and winks.  Then the light turns green, the driver makes his engine revs loudly, much to the amusement of his companions, and the car drives off in the distance.  Tom waits another few seconds in silence, then the zipper of his overstuffed luggage breaks open and all his  clothes tumble on the wet pavement.

					V.O
Where did it all start to go wrong?  When did I become another useless pawn in God’s almighty plan?  Was it at the very beginning?

C.U on a mother’s sweaty, groaning face, then zoom out to show a hospital room, the mother is giving birth, doctor is saying indistinct encouraging words, husband is filming with a video camera.  Another C.U on newborn baby boy.

					V.O
But that’s too early on.  Maybe it was then?

A sad ten-year-old kid waves goodbye to his friends.  Then we see him in a plane with his family.  Screen then shows a laid out map, and we see a picture of a plane traveling from Paris, France to New York.

					V.O
Or then?

C.U on a 21-year-old Tom at a party, smoking pot, empty bottles of beer all over the floor.

					V.O
But that’s too far ahead.  I think I’ve pinned down the time.  Let’s rewind a bit.

Moments from Tom’s life as a teenager being rewinded.

					V.O
There.  That’s it.  Senior Year of High School.  What I refer to now as “The Fall”.  That’s when my life tumbled, when I lost touch with reality.

The rewinding stops.  Tom, his parents, and his two siblings are standing in front of a big, white Victorian house.  A picket sign in the yard says, “House on sale.”  Furniture and boxes are being carried out and put in a large truck parked outside while a Mercedes convertible is being towed away.

					V.O
For the past two centuries people from all over the world had come to the US with nothing, some of them even managing to overcome the difficulties and build themselves a small fortune.

As V.O is being spoken, show images of waves of immigrants in 19th century coming from boats through Ellis Island.  Then show images of 10-year-old Tom and his family getting off plane and arriving at Kennedy Airport.

My parents had come to the US with millions, and in nine years they had managed to lose it all.  Talk about the fucking American Dream.

Return to first scene, Tom waiting for the T under the pouring rain, his luggage open and his clothes spread all over the ground.

					V.O
Let’s go back two weeks before this night.  It’s as good a place as any to start my story.

Fade to black.

EXT. BOSTON - DAY

Pink Floyd’s “Money” is playing.  It’s sunny.  Shots of college students walking along Commonwealth Ave.  Shots of Dorm buildings, a church, Classroom buildings.  Shot of a park, college students playing ultimate Frisbee.  Then C.U on a sign that reads, “welcome to Boston University.”  Then camera follows Tom walking in the street and heading back to his dorm building, Sleeper Hall.  He enters the building, goes to a wall full of mailboxes, opens his, takes out his mail, then we see Tom in the elevator, presses the button to the 8th floor, then he’s walking in a hallway, the door to his room is open, he enters it and finds his roommate, PAUL, a big Italian-American, sitting by his desk.  The song ends.

					Paul
Hey bro, wassup?

Tom is looking through his mail, stops at a letter with a BU logo on it.

					Tom
Fuck!

					Paul
Is it another eviction letter again?

					Tom
I’ll tell you in a sec.

Tom rips open the letter and skims through it.

Damn, doesn’t look like I’ll be your roommate for much longer.

					Paul
How long you fucking got?

					Tom
Two weeks and then I’m outta here.

A high-pitched scream from an adjacent room is heard.  Paul walks to the wall and pounds on it.

					Paul
MIKE, IF YOU DON’T SHUT THE FUCK UP, I’M GONNA COME OVER THERE WITH MY BUTCHER KNIFE AND SHOVE IT UP YOUR ASS!

Silence from the other side of the wall.

So, where you gonna go?

					Tom
Well, my sis.  She got an apartment over on Huntington.

Tom throws the rest of his mail on his desk, drops on his bed and sighs.

I’m so tired from all this fucking bullshit.  And on top of it, I’m so far behind in my work.  Yo, I gotta win like, 80 bucks by Saturday coz I got my Econ Midterm on Monday and I still haven’t bought the fucking textbook yet.

					Paul
				        (laughing)
Shit, that sucks bro.

					Tom
Who we playin’ with tonight, the track boys or the pot-heads?

					Paul
Potheads.

					Tom
Good, coz they suck.

CUT TO:

INT. STUDY ROOM - NIGHT

Six kids enter a study room and sit around a large table.  Playing with Tom and Paul are JOHN, STEVE, FISHER, and RICH.  Another kid is in the room, studying.  

					Paul
Hey, dickhead, why don’t you go study somewhere else, us grown-ups are about to play poker, and we don’t want your fucking negative study vibes perturbing us.

					Kid
Why don’t you go somewhere else?  I was here first.

Paul brusquely and violently gets up from his chair, which falls backward against the floor.  Paul walks up to the kid’s table, the kid shrinks back in his chair.  Paul bangs his two hands on the table.

					Paul
				(shouting, angry)
What the FUCK did you just say to me, motherfucker!?

					Kid
				(scared, stammering)
Well, I mean, I, I don’t have to leave, the room’s big enough for all of us.

Paul walks around to the kid’s seat, he grabs the kid by the collar, drags him to the door, and throws him out of the room.  Then he goes back to the kid’s table, picks up a graphic calculator, which he looks at, questioningly, then he puts the graphic calculator in his pocket.  Then he picks up the other books, goes back to the door and throws them out of the room.

					Paul
And stay the fuck out.  This is the Poker Room from now on; if I ever see you in here again, I’ll fuck you up so bad you’ll be going home in a body bag.

Paul walks back to his original table, where the five kids, laughing, witnessed the whole scene.  Paul sits down, takes out a ten-dollar bill, and puts it down on the table.

Let’s play some motherfucking poker.

CUT TO:

INT. STUDY ROOM - LATER SAME NIGHT

Thick cloud of smoke looms above the table.  There are now only five kids around the table, as Steve lost all his money and left.  Rich also lost everything but decided to stay.  They’re playing Texas Holdem.  Fisher is smoking pot.  He passes  it to Rich, who takes a puff, then offers it to Tom.

					Tom
Stop asking me every time, you know I don't touch that shit.

					Rich
You will someday, man.

					Paul
				(throws down his cards)
I’m out!

					John
	(throws some chips in a thick pot in the middle of the table, then looks at Tom)
I see your dollar and raise you another.

Tom looks at his cards, pondering.

C’mon.  I don’t have a great hand, I’m bluffing.  Besides, huh, I hear you need the money.

John, Rich and Fisher laugh.  Tom looks sharply at Paul.

					Paul
I didn’t say a fucking thing.  He came in the room and saw the letter you left on your desk.  I swear.

					Tom
		(looking down at his cards, whispers to himself)
OK.

Looks up at John.

All right, Johnny, all in.

Tom grins.  John stops laughing, shocked.  Fisher and Rich stop laughing, too, staring back and forth from Tom to John.  Paul just keeps looking at Tom.

					John
OK.  I’ll be nice and say your pot is about as big as mine.  I’m all in, too.  Show me what you got.

					Tom
				(puts down his cards)
Straight flush.

John’s smile disappears, and his face turns livid.

					Fisher
Well, show us what you got, John?

					John
				(throws his cards on the table)
Fuck you, Fish.

Rich picks up John’s two cards and looks at them.

					Rich
Ooooh, that sucks.  You lost with a fucking flush, man.  Tough.

					John
Fuck you, too, Rich.

Looks and points at Tom.

And fuck you, too.  I didn’t want to go all in, I’m taking my chips back.

John reaches for the pot to take his chips back, but Paul stops him with an arm.

					Paul
John, I showed you my butcher knife, right?  Now, you wanna make the 11 o’clock news?  I can see it already, “Poker game gone wrong as sore loser gets stabbed twenty times with giant butcher knife.”

John stares at Paul for a few seconds, then pulls his hands back from the pot, gets up, and leaves the room. 

CUT TO:

INT. DORM HALLWAY - LATER SAME NIGHT

Tom and Paul are leaving the study room and heading back to their room.  Tom’s holding a thick roll of bills in his hands.

					Tom
Remind me to never play again with those fuckers unless you’re there.  What a bunch of sore losers.  I mean, John, you know, I get it.  But Fish?  I wouldn’t have expected it from him.

					Paul
So how much money you got?  Enough to buy your textbook?

					Tom
Right now, I got 80.  So I’m 20 short.  But you know, now it means I can actually take Allison out to both a dinner and a movie.

Paul reaches for his wallet, takes out a 20-dollar bill, and gives it to Tom.

What are you doing?

					Paul
Well, as much as I think it’s sad that you have no sex life, and those 80 bucks would definitely help yours with Allison, I still think a midterm is more important.

					Tom
				(takes the 20-dollar bill)
Thanks, Paul.

					Paul
Well, let’s be honest here.  On a good day, with hours of make-up, Allison’s barely a 6.  And that’s being really, really, really nice.  She’s usually a 5.  Fuckable, yeah, but not worth wasting a midterm.  Now, if she were an 8, or, God forbid, a 9, then I’d say, fuck Econ.  Hell, if you hook up with an 8 or a 9, I’d walk home to New York just to let you have the room for the weekend.

					Tom
				        (perplexed)
Huh, thanks.  Don’t really think that’s a compliment, but whatever.  I’m fucking hungry, let’s go get some mozzarella sticks.

CUT TO:

INT. BARNES AND NOBLES - DAY

Tom is looking through rows of textbook shelves, looking for his econ textbook.  A pretty,  dark-haired girl, SONJA, is across the aisle from Tom, also searching for a textbook and nearing Tom.  Both notice the same textbook and go for it.  Tom grabs it first.

					Sonja
Excuse-me, I was gonna get that.

					Tom
So?  Get another one.

					Sonja
Yeah, well, you just took the last one.

					Tom
Well, sorry, but I need it for tomorrow's midterm.

					Sonja
And what the fuck do you think I need it for, dimwit?

					Tom
Well, look, since we both have the same midterm, why don’t we study together?

					Sonja
Mmm, let me think about it ... No.

					Tom
Fine, then.  Good luck explaining to Daddy why his precious is failing Econ.

Tom starts walking away.

					Sonja
Wait!  Fine, you win.  But who keeps the textbook after?

					Tom
Well, whoever pays for it.  Or, we can split it 50-50.  You keep it on weekends and holidays, and me during the week.

					Sonja
Deal.  Let’s go pay for it, then

They start walking toward the cash register.

					Tom
Yeah.  Hey, what dorm are you in?

					Sonja
Sleeper Hall.

					Tom
Oh cool, me, too.  Then we can meet to study at, say, 2 o’clock?  In the Poker Room?

					Sonja
The Poker Room?

					Tom
Oh, right.  Huh, second floor, the first lounge on the right coming out of the elevators.

Tom and Sonja split the textbook, each paying 50 bucks, then walk out of Barnes and Nobles.  Both stand immobile in the street.  Tom’s holding the bag with the textbook.

					Sonja
Look, I think I should keep the textbook till this afternoon.  Not that I don’t trust you, but, I don’t trust you.

					Tom
				(hands the bag to Sonja)
Whatever, take it.  You should probably get a head-start on the studying anyways, don’t want you to slow me down.

Sonja walks off.  Tom stands and stares at her walk, then when she’s out of sight, he goes off in the other direction.

CUT TO:

INT. CAFETERIA - SAME DAY

Tom grabs a slice of pizza, which he puts on his tray, already holding a plate of sausage and spaghettis.  Then he walks to a table to join his friend, D.

					D
So this mysterious girl, how do you know she’s not gonna run off with your textbook?

					Tom
I don’t.  I guess we’ll see this afternoon.

ALLISON, a slim red-haired girl, arrives and sits down next to Tom.

					Allison
What are you guys talking about?

					D
Huh, this beautiful, mysterious girl Tom met at Barnes and Nobles.

					Allison
					(vexed)
Oh.

					Tom
She’s not a beautiful, mysterious girl I just met.  She’s this girl I’m gonna study my econ midterm with, that’s all.  Look, Allie, I’m sorry for last week, by the way.

					Allison
Yeah, you still owe me a dinner and a movie.

					Tom
Well, you already got the movie.  I only owe you the dinner.  I got my midterm tomorrow, so I’m gonna study tonight, but if you’re free tomorrow night, I know this great Italian restaurant -

					Allison
Sure, I’d love to go.

					Tom
Cool.  I’ll call you tomorrow so we can meet up.  I gotta go study now.

					D
You’re not gonna eat?  Too impatient to meet the beautiful, mysterious girl?

					Tom
Shut the fuck up, D.  Not funny.  I’m just not hungry.  I never thought possible to say it, but this pasta tastes like shit.  And this (holds plate with slice of pizza, oil is dripping from plate), this is not pizza.  This is oil on bread.  I don’t know how you of all people, with your Italian heritage, can eat this crap.

					D
Yeah, whatever.  Oh, and before you go, on Sunday I’m going to 6 flags with some kids from Church, but we’re going like right after Mass.  Do you wanna come?  Coz if you do, you should come to Mass with me.

					Tom
Sorry, but as much as I love 6 flags, I have certain principles in life, and one of them is to never break a promise.  So, until the Fucker from above (points to the sky) gives me my three bucks back, I ain’t never setting foot in a church again.

					D
What three bucks?

					Tom
The three bucks your God stole from me when I was ten.

					D
I thought you didn't believe in God?

					Tom
God, the Church, the conspiracy, same difference, you know what I mean.

					D
And how did the Church steal three bucks from you?

					Tom
It was at my cousin’s wedding when I was ten.  I was sitting on the bench in the church with my family, and like this hat was being passed around, and you were supposed to put money into it.  Now, I thought the money would go to the newlywed couple, and I really like my cousin, so I put in all the money I had, which was like three bucks.  My father was puzzled coz he knows how much I fucking hate the church, so he asked me why I had given three bucks to the church.  I tried to get my money back, but they wouldn't let me.  So until I get my money back, and with interest, I ain't going to church again.  All right, gotta go.  See ya!

					Allison
Bye!

Tom walks away.

INT. POKER ROOM

Tom enters the room with a backpack strapped to his back.  He sees Sonja studying at a table, nose-deep in her books.  She doesn’t seem to notice him at first, and Tom stands still in the doorway, staring at her.

					Sonja
			   (still looking down at her books)
You’re late!

Tom enters the room, grinning, and sits across Sonja.

					Tom
Well, what can I say?  I was eating this amazing pizza in the cafeteria, and the best pasta I ever-

					Sonja
I don’t give a fuck.  Let’s study, shall we?

She looks up at him for the first time, giving him a malicious smile.

Now, do you have your class notes?

					Tom
Please, woman.  Who do you take me for?

Tom throws his grimy and torn backpack on the table, opens it, and rummages through it.  He can’t find the notes and Sonja drums her fingers on the table as a sign of impatience.

They’re in there somewhere.

He takes a large stack of ruffled papers and puts it on the table.

					Sonja
These are your Econ notes?

					Tom
Amongst other things, yes.  Now-

Pulls out a sheet from the stack. 

- here!  Supply and Demand.  Ever heard of that law? 

Sonja shakes her head in disbelief.

Now, do you have a boyfriend?

					Sonja
I don’t see the connection to our Econ midterm here.

					Tom
Oh, trust me, you will in a sec.  So, do you?

					Sonja
			    	      (mistrustful)
OK, then, no, I don’t have a boyfriend.

					Tom
No?  Good, then.  I mean, for my example.  Now, every single boy out there in the open  market is a potential supply for you.  Of course, in Econ you got outside forces, like price and quality and the time of year and whatever - all have a bearing on the equilibrium of the market.  Here, the outside forces are your personal preferences for men.  So, what kind attract you?

					Sonja
				(ponders for an instant)
Dark, short hair, not very tall.  Big and burly.

					Tom
So, like, a midget version of Sylvester Stallone?

					Sonja
					(smiling)
Yeah.

					Tom
I guess I don’t have a chance, then?

					Sonja
Wow!  So you’re not so stupid after all!

					Tom
So, like, no chance at all?  So if I wanted to invite you to dinner tomorrow night, to celebrate the amazing grade we’ll get on the midterm, you would obviously say no?

					Sonja
Obviously.  Now, c’mon, let’s get back to studying.  I need a good grade on this midterm.

Sonja dips her nose back into the textbook.

CUT TO:

INT. POKER ROOM - LATER SAME DAY

Tom and Sonja are both studying, surrounded by sandwich wrappings and empty coke cans.  Outside, dark has nearly fallen.  The room is silent until suddenly Tom’s phone vibrates.  Tom picks it up and reads his message.

					Tom
You should get outta here.

					Sonja
Why?

					Tom
Well, this ain’t called the Poker Room for nothing.  And it’s close to showtime.

					Sonja
What about you?  You’re gonna stay and play or you gonna keep studying?

					Tom
Me?  I’m staying.  I did enough studying to last a lifetime.  Anyway, money-wise, I’m kind of on the low side, and I got a date tomorrow night.

					Sonja
If I remember correctly, I said I wouldn’t go out with you tomorrow.

					Tom
And if I remember correctly, you ain’t the only girl on campus.  The market’s open for you, but it’s also for me.

Sonja gets up from her chair and puts her books back in her backpack.

					Sonja
Oh, is that so?  Me and my textbook are gonna go finish studying the last two chapters we haven’t even started looking at yet.  If I don’t see you at the exam, and I don’t intend to, good luck on the midterm.

					Tom
Right back atcha.

Sonja walks out of the Poker Room just as Paul and four other kids enter.  They join Tom and sit around the table.  Paul sits down next to Tom.

					Tom
				(to Paul, whispering)

Well, duh!  I told you, I’m a democrat.  I can’t stand Bush.  He’s bringing this country down.  And I mean, just look at the mess in Iraq.

					Tom
So you were against the war in Iraq?

					Allie
Damn right I was!  I even went to a rally in L.A.  Why?  Aren’t you against the war, too?

					Tom
Not really.  I mean, I’m not for wars in general.  I don’t want innocent people to die, you know?  But I mean, Saddam, well, he’s a piece of shit dictator who murdered a lot of people.  And from what I hear, his son, I don’t remember his name, but he’s gonna take over when Saddam dies, and apparently he’s crazy and a lot worse than Saddam himself.  I’m not saying as president I would have decided to attack Iraq, but as a world citizen, I can’t say I’m against that particular action.

					Allie
Wow.  You’re, like, the first person, or at least college student, that I actually meet and who’s for the war.  And you’re from New York, too.  That’s as democratic as it gets.

					Tom
What are you talking about?  D’s a lot more Republican than I am.  He’s as die-hard Republican as you are Democrat.  Me, I’m just moderate.  And I’m not saying I love Bush, or that I would have voted for him.  But I’m just saying that I particularly don’t think he’s doing such a bad job under the circumstances.

					Allie
So you think he went there for the Iraqis?  You’ve never heard of oil, have you?

					Tom
I’m not stupid, thank you.  But does it fucking matter what he went there for, as long as he did?  Take Lincoln, considered one of the greatest presidents of America, right?  But what has he really done?  Almost all his time spent in office was spent on war.

					Allie
Huh, Lincoln is a great president.  Are you insane?  He freed the slaves.

					Tom
Oh please, don’t bullshit a bullshitter.  Don’t tell me you think he went to war to free the slaves.  Do you know when the Civil War started?  In 1861.  Do you know when the Proclamation Declaration was passed?  1863.  Tell me, if he cared so much about the slaves, why did he wait two years?

					Allie
I don’t know.

					Tom
Well, let me tell you.  Coz he didn’t give a fuck, that’s why.  The only reason he did so is because he thought freeing the slaves would create some sort of revolt among the Blacks in the South, that they would rise against the Confederates and create chaos.  But the North was no heaven for Blacks.  Have you ever seen the movie Glory?  Based on a true story.  Northerners were as racist as Southerners, but what’s more disgusting about Northerners is that they were a bunch of hypocrites.  And so was Lincoln.

					Allie
And so’s Bush, then.  With his invented ‘weapons of mass destruction.’

					Tom
Yeah, you could argue that point.  But it’s not as hypocritical as you might think.  Today’s not like 1861.  Today you need a reason to declare war.  You can’t just attack anyone for no reason.  So he made one up.  Big deal.  A politician that lies, you’re gonna make a fuss about it?  Hell, a president that lies and you’re gonna make a fuss?  Huh, I have two words for you, Mrs. Democrat: Bill Clinton.  Who’s being a hypocrite now?

					Allie
Clinton’s lie didn’t kill anyone.  But thanks to Bush’ lies, hundreds of Americans have died, and who can say how many more will?  And I’m not even gonna start on the Iraqi casualties themselves.

					Tom
Yeah well, news-flash: wars are deadly.

					Allie
Yeah, that’s right.  That’s why I’m against war.

					Tom
Wow, no offense, but that’s the dumbest thing I’ve heard today.  You’re against war?  So you’re against the American Revolution?  You’re against the Americans fighting the Nazis in World War Two, or the North Koreans in the fifties?  Because all those were wars.

					Allie
Yeah, but that’s different.

					Tom
Yeah, how so?

					Allie
Because, I mean, those times there were good reasons to fight.

					Tom
Oh, right.  Goctha.  What you’re saying is, it’s good to save Jews being massacred by the Nazis, but it’s not good to save Shiites being massacred by Saddam’s regime.  Could you please explain to me why, because, personally, I just don’t get it?

					Allie
That’s not what I meant.  It’s just that, there are so many people in need of help.  I mean, what about Darfur?  What about North Korea?

					Tom 
Yeah, you’re right, and I wish people would do something about those places, too, instead of pussying out.  But your reasoning is retarded.  You’re saying that because we can’t save everyone, we shouldn’t save anyone.  That’s stupid.  All right, this conversation has gone far enough.  This is your stop, anyway.

They arrive in front of Allison’s dorm, and both stop, silent, heads looking down.

					Allie
Well, thanks for the dinner.  It was an entertaining and enlightening night.

					Tom
 				           (grins)
Yeah.  Sorry if I offended or insulted you.  Sometimes I get drawn in these conversations and I become a bit over-excited and … whatever.  I’m sorry.

					Allie
No, don’t be.  I mean, you’re entitled to your political convictions.

					Tom
Damn right I am!

					Allie
However wrong they may be.

					Tom
All right, I think it’d be best if I left.  See you.

					Allie
Yeah, bye.

Tom turns away, crosses the street, and heads toward Sleeper Hall.  Allie stands still a bit, looks at Tom cross the street, then she herself turns and enters her building.

CUT TO: 

INT. SLEEPER HALL - LATER SAME NIGHT

Tom looks at his watch, which indicates it’s 1 A.M.  He grins and heads toward the poker room, where five kids, including Paul, are playing poker.  The other kids are Rich, Steve, Fisher, and John.

					Tom
Hey ladies!  Deal me in next game.  I spent all my dough on a fucking democrat and I’m broke so I need to make some cash quickly.

					Paul
So how was your date?

					Tom
Wasn’t that bad.  Although I don’t think Allie had much fun.

					Paul
Why not?

					Tom
Well, I totally forgot she was a vegetarian, and I took her to a restaurant who turns out to be anti-vegetarian.  Then on the way back we got into a political debate about Iraq and I came pretty close to calling her stupid.  In fact, I’m pretty sure I did call her stupid.  And retarded, too.

					Paul
Seems like fun.  Now at least she must have gotten the message that you don’t like her.


CUT TO:

INT. TOM’S ROOM, SLEEPER HALL - THREE DAYS LATER

Paul and Tom are both studying in their rooms, listening to Led Zeppelin’s Dazed and Confused.

					Tom
				         (yawning)
Awaaaahhhhh, I’m so tired of fucking studying.  Let’s take a Halo break.

					Paul
Yeah, OK.  You set it up, I’ll go see if Fish and Steve wanna play.

Paul leaves the room while Tom turns the TV and the X-box on.  Paul comes back thirty seconds later, alone.

Fuckers don’t wanna play.  They’re “studying”.

					Tom
Well, Paul, you have to be considerate.  These are stupid people, they’re not smart like us.  If they don’t study, they get bad grades.  

Paul laughs.

By the way, you still wanna leave Saturday morning?  Coz if you wanna take the bus with me, I’m leaving, like, really early.

					Paul
Like, what time?  9 A.M?

					Tom
No, I’m taking the 7 A.M bus.  And since it’s in Chinatown, we have to leave at, like, 6 .

					Paul
Yeah, OK.  Count me in, bro.

CUT TO:

INT. BUS - MORNING, TWO DAY LATER

Paul and Tom are sitting in a crowded bus next to each other, the bus racing down an empty I-95.

					Paul
So, you still haven’t heard from Sonja since she cancelled on you?

					Tom
Nope.  Called her and left her like 10 messages, but nada.

					Paul
Well, whatever, bro.  What about Allie?

					Tom
Yeah, I have lunch with her and D almost everyday.  She wants to go out with me again.  I told her I couldn’t because of midterms, and then this week I’m home for the break, so I won’t have to deal with her.  And then, when I come back, I won't even be on campus anymore, so that kind of settles everything.

					Paul
Well you can still come over whenever you want.  I have an uncle back home who’s a locksmith, I’ll ask him to make a double of my key, I’ll give it to you.

					Tom
Yeah, but did you forget that we have to swipe in our card to get in the building?  So they’ll know my every move.  It’s like, they think they’re Big Brother or something.

					Paul
Big Brother?  What’s that?

					Tom
Never heard of 1984?

					Paul
Sorry, I was born in '85.  A year off.

					Tom
Wha-, we read the fucking book for class in November.

					Paul
No, you did.  How do you think I got a 69 on my finals?

					Tom
Whatever.  By the way, what're you doing on Wednesday?

					Paul
I don’t know.  Don’t have anything planned for the break yet, just gonna hang with my girl, that’s all.

					Tom
If you’re not doing anything, you should come to Manhattan Ville College, I’m playing there with my band.  It’s like a Battle of the Band thing, the crowd votes for the best band.  So come with your girlfriend, that way I can meet her, and that way my band gets two votes.

					Paul
Sorry to break it to you, bro, but you ain’t buying votes like that.  I’ll only vote for you if I think your band deserves them.  If anyone’s better than you, then I ain’t voting for you.

					Tom
Well, I'll get your girlfriend's vote then.

					Paul
My girlfriend?  She a woman.  She votes for who I tell her to vote.

Suddenly Tom and Paul hear a police siren from behind them.  The bus keeps going for a few seconds then pulls over on the side of the highway.  Tom, Paul, and all the passengers are bewildered.  Through the windows Tom sees a police officer walk by the side of the bus, then tap on the bus door.  The door opens.

					Officer
Sir, would you please step out of the vehicle?

The driver, a short Chinese man in his mid-fifties, looks at the cop without budging.

					Driver
				(thick Chinese accent)
What is problem, officer?

					Officer
Sir, please, step out of the vehicle.

					Driver
But what is problem?

					Officer
The problem, sir, is that you were going 100/mph with a bus full of passengers.  Now, please, step out of the vehicle.

					Driver
I no understand.  What is problem?

					Officer
				        (exasperated)
Sir, this is your last warning, step out of the vehicle now.

					Driver 
I no understand.  What is problem?

The police officer steps inside the bus.  He’s tall and has to bend so he doesn’t bang his head on the ceiling.

					Officer
				(slow and articulate)
Sir, do you speak English?

					Driver
				(smiles and nods his head)
Yes, I speak English.

					Officer
All right.  Sir, do you know what the speed limit is?

					Driver
I no speeding.

					Officer
That’s not what I’m asking you.

Police officer grunts.

You don't understand a word I’m saying, do you?

					Driver
				  (exasperated, angry)
Yes, I speak English, you motherfucker!

CUT TO:

EXT. BUS – MINUTES LATER

Bus driver is being led, handcuffed, to the police car.  The driver is agitated and seemingly angry, but we see the scene from Tom's point of view inside the bus so we don't hear the driver's comments.

					Paul
That's one crazy Chinaman, bro.

CUT TO: 

CHINATOWN, NEW YORK - LATER SAME DAY

Tom and Paul are out of the bus, walking in the busy and crowded streets of New York’s Chinatown.

					Tom
Well, that was the worst bus ride I ever had.

 					Paul
It wasn’t that bad.  Quite fun, when you think about it.  How many times do you see your bus driver arrested?

					Tom
Yeah, well, I don’t give a shit if it’s funny.  When I pay for a 3 hour drive from Boston to New York, I expect to get to New York in 3 hours.  We had to wait a fucking hour and a half on the side of the highway.  I’m gonna ask for my money back.  Do you remember the name of the company?

					Paul
I don’t know.  It was written in Chinese.  I don’t read Chinese.

					Tom
Yeah, well no shit, Sherlock, you don’t even read English.  All right, this is my stop.

					Paul
Going to Grand Central to take the train, right?

					Tom
Yup.  I got another good hour, hour and a half of travel.  So I’ll see you in two weeks.  I’ll have to come by and pick my shit to bring it over to my sister’s place.

					Paul
Yeah, just give me a call when you get there.  Anyway, I’ll probably come on Wednesday to your Battle of the Band thing.  See ya, bro.

					Tom
Yeah, see ya.

Tom struggles down the stairs into the subway, carrying a large and heavy duffel bag, while Paul walks away down the street with his rolling suitcase.

CUT TO:

EXT. LARCHMONT TRAIN STATION - EARLY AFTERNOON

Tom is on the platform looking around the parking lot for a beat-up Mitsubishi.  He finds it, grins and walks there.  He's walking at a fast pace, carrying his duffel bag, and at the same time looking sideways at the car.  Just as he's turning his head to look forward again, he walks straight into a pole and bangs his nose.  Blood flows out and stains his coat.

CUT TO:

INT. CAR ON BEACH TREE DRIVE - MINUTES LATER

The Mitsubishi turns on a dead-end street and approaches a large house, pulls into its driveway, and stops.  Tom and Mom get out of the car.

CUT TO:

INT. HOUSE, DINING ROOM - NIGHT

The family is having dinner around a large, rectangular table in the dining room.  There’s a big chandelier hanging from the ceiling, right above the table, lighting the place.  At the head of the table is Mom; on the right side is DAD, a fifty-two year-old dark haired man of average height; next to him is WILL, Tom’s seventeen year-old brother.  Opposite them are Tom and Geri.

					Dad
				       (In French)
So, Tom, I'm waiting for your report card to see the good grades you've been getting.

					Geri
Yeah, well, don't hold your breath on that.

					Dad
Why?

					Geri
Well, because gambling is not a class, and that's all he does 24/7.

					Tom
				          (grinning)
Actually, get your facts straight.  I play as much videogames than I do poker.

					Dad
You think this is a joke?  We're talking about your future here.  Do you know how expensive your school is?  You better get some good grades.

					Tom
Actually, I do know how expensive my school is.  And guess what?  You don't have the money to pay for it, that's why I'm getting kicked out of dorms, so if I were you, I'd shut up about it.  And it's not like Ratty Bitch there (points and looks at Geri) is doing any better.  She doesn't play poker, true, but she's wasted all the time.  The other day she was so drunk she passed out after puking all over her room.

					Mom
Who the hell do you think you are?  You don't talk to your father that way; apologize right now!

					Dad
No, it's all right.  They're vulgar and talk back to me all the time, what do you expect, that's how you raised them.

					Mom
				(takes out a cigarette and lights it)
Fuck you, OK?  Just leave me alone, all right?  What about you, huh?  Why didn't you raise them better?

Mom gets up and leaves the table.

					Geri
Yeah, mom didn't raise us badly, you did.  You never help around the house.  All you do is moan all day long.

					Dad
Shut up, OK?  I'm not talking to you.  We'll see what kind of grades you get.  You better be getting straight A's.

					Will
Yeah, coz Geri, look who's talking?  You're the laziest, most selfish person here.  You never fucking help.

					Geri
				(takes out a cigarette)
Yeah, you're right, I don't.  Why should I, you're all assholes?

					Dad
You're not gonna smoke now, are you?

					Geri
Yeah, I am.  I'm 21, I can do whatever I want.

					Dad
I'm eating my dinner here, so you're not gonna smoke.

					Geri
Huh, yeah, I am.  You can't tell me what to do.

					Tom
Yeah, well, it's called manners.  We're eating dinner here.  It's not because you're an anorexic bitch that you have to piss everyone off.

Geri lights her cigarette, takes a puff, and blows the smoke towards Tom's plate.

					Geri
Well, I guess I don't have any manners.

					Tom
You're lucky I'm not your father, coz otherwise I'd smack the shit out of you.

					Geri
Yeah, well, too bad, isn't it?

					Tom
I'm gonna go eat in the kitchen.

Tom gets up from the table with his plate.  On his way he walks by Geri's seat, and he picks up her cigarette pack, which lay on the table.

					Geri
Hey!  Give it back to me.

					Tom
					(grins)
Yeah, right.  If you want it back, you'll find it in the trash.


CUT TO:

EXT. COMMONWEALTH AVE. - LATE AFTERNOON

Tom is in the lobby of Sleeper Hall.  He takes his phone and calls Paul.

					Tom
Hey, are you in the room?  … All right, I’m gonna come over now to pick up my shit… yeah, see ya.

CUT TO:

INT. SLEEPER HALL, PAUL’S ROOM - NIGHT

Tom has a suitcase packed, waiting by the door, along with his held-hand Sony stereo.

					Tom
I guess I’ll come sometime this week for the rest of my stuff, coz I don’t wanna be going back and forth all night under this weather.

					Paul
Yeah, sure bro.  You sure you don’t want me to help you carry your things to your sister’s?

					Tom
Thanks for the offer, but it’s fine.

					Paul
All right.  Well, come back whenever, bro.  It’s still your room.

					Tom
Thanks.  See ya.

CUT TO:

EXT. COMMONWEALTH AVE. - NIGHT

Back to opening scene, Tom waiting in the rain for the T-train.  His suitcase is open and his clothes are spread all over the wet floor, rain still pouring.  Thick headlights are visible in the distance, approaching.  It’s the train coming.  Tom hurries picking up his clothes and shoves them back in his suitcase.

CUT TO:

INT. GERI’S APARTMENT - LATER SAME NIGHT

Tom walks along a narrow, dirty hallway.  A torn, grimy mattress is posed along one of the walls, empty bags of chips and cans of coke cover the floor here and there.  Tom gets to a door and knocks.  A few seconds later, Geri opens the door.

					Geri
What the hell took you so long?  You said you’d be here an hour ago.

					Tom
					(sighs)
Yeah well, not my fault if everything we own is fucking broken.

					Geri
What the hell are you talking about?

					Tom
Oh, you wanna see?

Tom walks in.  The apartment has four rooms: a windowless main room lit by a dizzying yellow light bulb.  There’s a kitchenette, with a dirty sink, no oven.  Opposite of it is the room’s sole furniture, a used, torn couch.  There are three doors that lead to the apartment’s three bedrooms.  There’s a fourth door that leads to the bathroom, which is even dirtier than the rest of the apartment.  The stains in the bathtub look like dry vomit.  Geri’s room is the door on the far right.  Tom walks in Geri’s room and opens his suitcase.  Geri follows her brother and sees all the wet clothes.

					Geri
Damn.

CUT TO:

EXT. APARTMENT BUILDING -- NIGHT

Tom is waiting outside a building.  He sees Paul walk up to him and grins.

					Tom
Hey, what's up?

					Paul
Hey.  Thanks for inviting me, bro.

					Tom
No problem.  My sis invited me, and I didn't wanna go with just her, coz she's gonna be with her new boyfriend, some guy named Bill or whatever.  All right, let's go in.

CUT TO:

INT. APARTMENT -- NIGHT

Tom and Paul enter the apartment, Hip-hop music being played.   The place is small, only two rooms, but it's pretty crowded, and in the bigger room a few girls are dancing on the "dance floor."  Tom and Paul walk through the apartment, grab themselves a drink along the way, and sit next to a girl on a couch right in front of the dance floor.

A FEW MINUTES LATER:

Paul and the girl on the couch are making out, Tom is wasted and just sitting.  The girl on the couch gets up and goes to the bathroom.

					Paul
Bro, you gotta get some action.  Go dance with those girls over there.

					Tom
Nah.

					Paul
All right, what if I get one of them to come here, will you talk to her?

					Tom
Yeah, OK, but if you do, try to get the one in the red shirt, the others aren't that great.

Paul gets up and heads to the dance floor to talk to the girls in the crowd.  At the same time, a black guy, Jimmy, comes to sit down next to Tom.

					Jimmy
Don't I know you?

Tom looks at Jimmy for a second.

					Tom
Yeah, I think I remember you.  Oh, I know: FASNY, right?

					Jimmy
Damn, that's right man.  Wow, that was ages ago.

A beautiful brunette, Kate, sits next to Tom on the couch and interrupts his conversation.

					Kate
Hi.  I'm Kate.

					Tom
Oh, huh, Hi.  I'm Tom.

Tom turns back to Jimmy and shifts the position of his legs at the same time.  While doing so, some beer spills from his glass onto Kate's skirt.  Kate jumps up.

					Kate
				(screaming, angry)
Fuck!  You moron!

Jimmy and Tom both laugh.

					Tom
				(trying to stop laughing)
Shit, I'm really sorry.

Kate storms off.

MINUTES LATER:

Tom is standing in the middle of the crowd, dazed and with a drink in his hand.  Geri approaches him, followed by a short, skinny guy, BILL.

					Geri
Hey, Tom

Geri reaches Tom, but at the same time her phone rings.  She picks it up and starts walking away.  Bill and Tom are left facing each other.

					Bill
Hey, I'm Bill.

					Tom
You're Bill?  Damn, my sister's tastes keeps getting worse and worse.

Bill's face reddens with embarrassment, he doesn't know what to say.  Tom keeps squinting and struggles just standing up, but nonetheless he takes a large gulp from his glass.

Are you rich?

					Bill
Excuse-me?

					Tom
I said, are you rich?

					Bill
No, not really.  I mean, especially compared to some of the kids who live here.

					Tom
Oh.  Then you must be a funny guy.  Tell me a joke.

					Bill
What?

					Tom
Well, you're not rich and you're ugly – no offense, by the way, you just are – so you must be fucking hilarious.  I mean, my sister dates a lot of guys, and by a lot I mean, like, a shitload, but still, she doesn't date the biggest losers right off the street.  Or not until you, at least.

					Bill
OK, I think someone had a bit too much to drink, there.

					Tom
Hey!  I'm not drunk.

					Bill
Yeah, OK.

					Tom
Man, you don't know shit from fuck.  If I were drunk, could I do this?

Still holding his beer in one hand, Tom attempts to put one foot after the other in a straight line, at the same time extending his arms to keep his balance.  At the same time he does so, Kate, not looking, walks straight into his arm holding his beer, and the beer spills all over her top.  

Whoops.

					Kate
Oh, my, God.  I'm gonna fucking kill you.

Kate randomly takes someone's glass and shoves it at Tom, then she walks away.  People around start laughing, including Bill.

					Tom
				           (at Bill)
Hey!  Fuck you, Funnyman.  You wanna take it outside?  That's what I thought.

There's a heavy knock on the front door, almost like a thump.

					Voice
Police!  Open up!

					Tom
Oh, look, it's the police, Bill.  You better run; they're here to arrest you coz you're ugly, poor, and not funny.

Someone by the door opens the door and two heavy officers enter the room.

					Police Officer
All right, Party's over!  Turn the music off!

Someone turns the music off.

I want everyone out of here in 5 minutes.  Get moving, people!

CUT TO:

EXT. STREET – NIGHT

C.U on Tom's face.

					Tom
You know, I've always hated banks, I don't know why.

C.U on Paul's face.

					Paul
Yeah, me too.

Paul smiles and nods.  C.U on Tom's face, who's also smiling and nodding.

					Tom
Wait!  Isn't your dad a banker?

C.U on Paul's face.

					Paul
Oh yeah.  I fucking hate my father, too.

					Voice
Actually, I hate banks, too.

C.U on Tom, who leans past Paul to see who spoke.

					Paul
				(looking at the man on his left)
Who the fuck are you?

C.U on Bill's face.

					Bill
I'm Bill.

C.U on Tom's face.

					Tom
Shouldn't you be with my sister?

C.U on Bill's face.

					Bill
She left the party with another guy.

C.U on Tom's face.

					Tom
Big fucking surprise there.  But you shouldn't feel too bad, at least you lasted longer than the last one.  All right, I'm done here.

C.U on Paul's face.

					Paul
Yeah, me too.

Sound of zippers being closed, then a zoomed out shot of Tom, Paul, and Bill standing in front of a CityBank, a large puddle at their feet.

SCENE I
On one side of the stage, Lu lays in the bed, awake. Tom and Meg sit by a small table playing chess. Mike is sleeping beside. There’s one telephone on the table.
On the other side of the stage in the dark there’s another telephone on a small table. 

LIGHTS UP ON: LU, TOM AND MEG.

(after a few second of silence)

LU
((sighing) )
I can't believe he's gay.

TOM
((to Lu))
I told you so.

MEG
Well, I guess we made him come out.

TOM
WE made it? You mean, YOU made it.

LU
We made it? What are you talking about?

MEG
I mean, we turned him gay.

TOM
Again with this “we” bullshit. YOU did it.

LU
But.. that's impossible! It's not our fault! I mean.. nobody can really turn anybody gay.. right?

TOM
That's right: nobody can. Except you. Trust me, I know from experience: you would have turned Saddam Hussein gay.

MEG
((To Tom))
That's mean. People can actually turn others gay.
((to Lu) )
And you can't say that it's our FAULT: it's not a sin, to be gay.
